claims.statement: The checked-in HTTP contract is openapi/powercontext.yaml, an OpenAPI 3.0.3 document at API version 1.5.2 that defines every /v1 path, schema, header, and status code.

The Python generated models, operation metadata, and schema under src/powercontext/http/_generated are produced by scripts/generate_api.py from openapi/powercontext.yaml and must not be hand-edited; make api-generate writes them and make api-generate-check fails on drift, and contract-test runs the check.

The running Server serves its OpenAPI document at /openapi.json (omitted when the app is infrastructure-only) and a public Scalar reference at /docs, and the served document is the canonical generated schema with the /v1/handoff-reports paths removed unless Handoff Reports are enabled.

Authentication applies to every external HTTP request except a fixed public allowlist (/, /docs, /health/live, /health/ready, and the remote Skill target enroll, reconcile, package download, and receipt routes); /openapi.json is not public and requires a bearer token.

The contract declares BearerAuth as the default security requirement and TargetBearerAuth for remote Skill target reconcile, package download, and receipt routes, which are separate from user Principal authentication.

A rejected bearer credential returns 401 with code unauthorized and a WWW-Authenticate Bearer challenge, and a failing or unreachable authentication provider returns 503 with code authentication_unavailable; both use the error envelope with code, message, and details, with details null.

GET /v1/connection/identity reports the deployment's authentication mode (disabled or authenticated) and the request Principal under access.self without invoking readiness probes, and grants no resource permission; anonymous identity is reported only when both authentication and access enforcement are disabled.

GET /health/ready returns HTTP 200 when readiness checks pass, and returns 503 with status not_ready when the Runtime readiness probe fails or when an enforced access or authentication provider is not ready.

Generic Artifact heads carry a strong ETag derived from the current revision in the form "revision:N", returned on reads and writes, and GET /v1/scopes/{scope_id}/artifacts/{family}/{artifact_id} answers If-None-Match with 304 and the same ETag when the head is unchanged.
PUT /v1/scopes/{scope_id}/artifacts/{family}/{artifact_id} requires If-Match; a missing If-Match is rejected with 428 precondition_required before any Runtime call is made.

A replacement whose If-Match does not equal the current head ETag returns 412 with code revision_conflict and details containing provided_etag and current_etag; the storage layer re-checks the expected ETag inside the write transaction so a concurrent commit also yields 412 rather than a silent overwrite.
Artifact tag replacement requires If-Match, and a stale tag ETag returns 412 with code tag_precondition_failed.
Atomic Memory content replacement uses the same revision-derived content ETag, while Atomic lifecycle and state operations are conditioned on a state_version that is separate from the content ETag.

Handoff is a Scope singleton: POST /v1/scopes/{scope_id}/artifacts with family handoff returns 409 with code artifact_already_exists and details use_replace true when a Handoff already exists, and callers must update it through the replace route with If-Match.

Legacy Memory collection operations (citation reads and mutations, collection capacity and changes, and non-null collection revision preconditions) return 422 with code legacy_memory_operation_unsupported, listing Atomic Memory alternatives and instructing callers not to drop collection CAS preconditions or retry automatically.

Every HTTP response carries X-PowerContext-Dream-Contract: 2. On the fixed legacy response paths, a request without that header is projected to the legacy shape, and a 2xx JSON response containing a Dream-only shape that cannot be projected is replaced by 426 client_upgrade_required, except that refine_experience and derive_skill remain compatible without the header; error responses pass through unchanged.

The Python Client sends X-PowerContext-Dream-Contract: 2 on its requests, and the MCP internal bridge sends the same header, so first-party clients satisfy the Dream contract without caller configuration.

Every HTTP response carries X-PowerContext-Request-ID, whose value is the bound request identifier for internal bridge calls or otherwise the current tracing span's 16-hex identifier, and never an inbound X-Request-ID header; the access log records one completion per external HTTP request and skips health probes, metrics, the MCP path, and internal bridge calls.
The MCP surface is mounted at /mcp only when MCP is enabled, as a stateless Streamable HTTP application that issues no MCP session identifiers.
MCP tools are generated from the OpenAPI document by operationId, and only operations listed in the curated MCP operation set are exposed; prepare_context and flush are not MCP tools.

MCP tools carry read-only, destructive, or idempotent annotations so hosts can apply confirmation policy, but these hints are not an authorization boundary because the MCP call traverses the same HTTP routes and their Access checks.

MCP get_artifact and replace_artifact return an envelope of artifact, etag, and status_code, where a conditional 304 yields artifact null with the current etag, and MCP replace_artifact accepts only family atomic-memory and requires the etag from get_artifact as If-Match.
The MCP server reaches the application through an in-process ASGI bridge that marks the request as internal, reuses the logical request identifier, and counts a tool call once in the access log.
Review writes on /v1/candidates/list, get, history, revise, approve, and reject are POST operations, and the write operations require the current expected_version.
Creating an Artifact through POST /v1/scopes/{scope_id}/artifacts returns 201 with a Location header and an ETag for revision one, and returns 409 when the Scope singleton already exists.
